neighbours.label: an amount or lack of a usable supply of something (plenty of wood, enough money, no bread left, nothing, nobody), read on the supply noun or 'left' and strongest on a following 'to'/'for' saying what it is for (plenty of wood to burn, nothing to do, enough room for, de quoi, para); quiet for the same noun without an amount word (the firewood to burn, a space for), for a plain verb 'to' (wants to), and for direction or recipient 'to'/'for' (walked to, a gift for)
neighbours.short: amount/lack of a usable supply, + 'to'/'for' its use
fire: We had plenty of wood to burn through the whole winter.
There is nothing to do in this town after nine o'clock.
Do you have enough money for the bus fare home?
By Friday there was no bread left for the children's lunches.
She found nobody to help her carry the boxes upstairs.
The new apartment has enough room for a piano and two desks.
Il n'y a pas de quoi manger dans le frigo.
No tengo tiempo suficiente para terminar el informe.
quiet: We stacked the firewood to burn in the shed by the barn.
He wants to leave this town after nine o'clock.
Do you have the bus card I gave you yesterday?
On Friday she walked to the bakery for the children's lunches.
She asked her brother to carry the boxes upstairs.
The new apartment has a space for a piano near the window.
Il est allé à Paris pour voir sa sœur.
Le compré un regalo para su cumpleaños.
